transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is my eating has gotten really off. Some days I barely manage coffee and maybe a granola bar before work, and my scrubs are starting to hang loose on me. I’m not trying to lose weight, so it’s been worrying me.
Have you lost weight without trying to?
Yeah, I think so. My scrubs have been getting looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight. I just haven’t been eating much—some days it’s just coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
No, not really. I’m not worried about gaining weight. It’s more that I just don’t feel like eating much lately.
Do you find that food doesn't taste as good to you as it used to?

I don’t know if it’s the taste exactly. It’s more like I just don’t feel like eating. I’ll get to work and realize I’ve only had coffee and maybe a granola bar, and lately my scrubs are fitting looser, even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
Do you feel like you have no interest in eating at all?

Not no interest at all, but it’s pretty close some days. I just don’t feel like eating, and before a shift I might only manage coffee and a granola bar. My scrubs are hanging looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
How much weight would you say you've lost since you first noticed your eating habits change?

I’m not exactly sure in pounds. I haven’t really been weighing myself. I just know my scrubs are fitting a lot looser, and it started after my eating got so off—some days it’s just coffee and maybe a granola bar before work.
Have you noticed a decrease in enjoyment of activities you usually like to do?

Yeah. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends… stuff like that. Lately I just tell myself there’s no point, and I end up sitting at home scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet instead.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
Yeah… I have. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, kind of hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even get going or put on my badge.
Would you say you've lost a significant amount of weight, like more than 5% of your body weight, since your eating habits changed?

I don’t know the exact percentage. I haven’t really weighed myself. But yeah, it feels like a lot—my scrubs are hanging looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight. Some days I’m barely getting down coffee and a granola bar before a shift.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when you think about eating or when you're actually eating?
I don’t think so, no. I’m not really scared of eating or uncomfortable with the food itself. I just… don’t have much appetite, and eating feels like effort sometimes.
Is your lack of interest in eating similar to your lack of interest in other activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, it’s pretty similar. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends… stuff I actually liked. Now I mostly just think, “What’s the point?” and end up at home scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet. Eating kind of feels like that too—just hard to care enough to do it.
Has your weight loss been so significant that others have noticed or commented on it?

Yeah, a couple people have noticed. Someone at work mentioned my scrubs looked kind of baggy, and I can feel it too. I’m not trying to lose weight—it’s just that my eating’s been off, like some days it’s just coffee and maybe a granola bar before work.
Do you think you would feel like eating more if you weren't feeling so sad or depressed?

Yeah, I think so. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even get my badge on. When I’m in that place, eating just feels like one more thing I don’t have it in me to do.
Did you start feeling sad and depressed before your eating habits changed, or did it happen after?

The sadness came first, I think. The eating changed after that. The steady depressed feeling and not caring about things really settled in later, and it’s been going on for about… a year and four months now.
How long have you been feeling like you don't care about the things you used to enjoy?
It’s been about a year and four months, I’d say. The not caring about things kind of settled in with the depression, and it’s just been there pretty steadily since then.
How long have you been feeling like you don't want to eat?

It’s been long enough that it’s noticeable now. I’m not sure exactly when it started, but lately some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before work. My scrubs are getting loose, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
How long have you been feeling like you don't want to eat?

Like I said, I can’t pin down exactly when it started. It’s just gotten bad enough lately that before work I might only manage coffee and a granola bar, and my scrubs are fitting loose now even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
How long have you been feeling like you don't want to eat?

I don’t have an exact start date. It’s just gotten to the point where some days before a shift I barely manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and my scrubs are hanging loose now even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
How many months have you been feeling like you don't want to eat?
I’d say it’s been a few months. I don’t know the exact number, but long enough that my appetite being off is obvious, and my scrubs are fitting loose now.
How many months ago did you first notice you weren't wanting to eat as much?

Probably a few months ago. I can’t give you the exact month, but that’s when I started noticing I wasn’t eating much—some days just coffee and a granola bar before work, and then my scrubs started fitting looser.
